7 Concrete online marketing tips for construction companies - Komate

# 7 Concrete online marketing tips for construction companies who want to grow.

You work hard, deliver quality, and your customers are satisfied. But how do you make sure more people can find you? How do you ensure you're not just getting customers through word-to-mouth, but are also visible online for new projects?

Good news: You don't need to be a marketing specialist to achieve results. With a few smart, accessible steps, you can accomplish a lot as a construction company. Here are 7 concrete marketing tips you can implement today:

**Inhoud**

*   [1\. Update your Google Business Profile.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#Google_business)
*   [2\. Show your projects on socials.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#projects)
*   [3\. Collect client reviews.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#client_reviews)
*   [4\. Clear and professional website.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#website)
*   [5\. Be found on Google.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#Google)
*   [6\. Start small with Google Ads.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#Google_Ads)
*   [7\. Share your knowledge.](https://www.komate.be/en/blog/7-concrete-online-marketing-tips-for-construction-companies#knowledge)

 ![](/getmedia/45237801-c753-4f5f-960a-88cfd927a730/Bouwbedrijven-en-online-marketing-\(2\)_1.jpg)

## 1\. Update your Google Business Profile.

Your Google Business Profile (formerly Google My Business) is **often the first thing people see** when they Google you name or services. A well-filled-out profile ensures that you're found more easily locally, and it helps you appear trustworthy.

Make sure to include:

*   Correct address and contact information
*   Opening hours (even if they're flexible)
*   Recent project photos
*   A brief description of what you do

**BONUS**: Ask satisfied customers for a Google Review!

 ![](/getmedia/550df81c-342f-45a4-ac90-f071bdb3965f/Scherm%c2%adafbeelding-2025-04-29-om-16-37-48.png)

## 2\. Show projects on socials.

Before-and-after photos of your work always perform well. Not only do they showcase your craftsmanship, but they also highlight the types of projects you handle.

What works well:

*   A short description of the project
*   Location & type of work (e.g., "Renovation of family home in Zwolle")
*   Photos of the process or the final result

**Consistency is key**: 1 post per week can make a significant difference in visibility.

## 3\. Collect client reviews.

Satisfied customers are your best salespeople. Ask them for a review on Google or request a short testimonial that you can use on your website and social media.

**TIP**: Ask for specific feedback, such as "What did you think of the collaboration?" or "What stood out positively during the project?"

Post the reviews:

*   On your homepage
*   In quotes or proposals
*   Under project descriptions

 ![](/getmedia/1939b162-f1b0-4131-83d5-53d9306d430d/2_1.jpg)

 ![](/getmedia/c86de280-1c6f-40b8-8526-4174321e625e/4.jpg)

## 4\. Clear and professional website.

Your website is often your first impression. If it's outdated, potential customers will move on. You don't need a complicated site, but it should be clear and trustworthy.

Essential on your website:

*   A clear description of your services
*   Project photos + references
*   Contact information and an easy-to-use form
*   A strong call-to-action (e.g., "Request a free quote")

## 5\. Be found on Google.

Even if you're not advertising, you can still be easily found, as long as you use the right keywords on you website. Think of terms like:

*   "Carpenter Antwerp"
*   "Dormer installation in Ghent"
*   "1930s home renovation"

Use those keywords in your pages, headings, and image names.

**EXTRA TIP**: Add a FAQ section with questions that customers often ask. It's good for SEO and for your visitors.

## 6\. Start small with Google Ads.

If you want to be found faster, Google Ads is a powerful tool. You only advertise to people who are already actively searching for what your offer - perfect.

Start small:

*   Choose a few services + regions
*   Set a daily budget
*   Direct visitors to a clear page on your website

Keep it simple, track results, and gradually scale up if it works.

 ![](/getmedia/08f4acdb-03a0-4f97-be3c-0759b1383349/Scherm%c2%adafbeelding-2025-04-30-om-13-57-56.png)

 ![](/getmedia/35c60db9-8fd3-4858-b735-634c6513d3f3/Scherm%c2%adafbeelding-2025-04-30-om-13-58-43.png)

## 7\. Share your knowledge.

People are not only looking for a skilled professional but also for someone who thinks ahead. Show this online by sharing tips:

*   "5 things to consider when renovating"
*   "When is it smart to replace your roof?"
*   "Our checklist for a stress-free renovation"

This type of short content can be posted on your website, social media, or even as a free download (which can also help you gather leads!).

### Ready to grow?

Online marketing doesn't have to be complicated. With these 7 steps, you can appear more professional, be found more easily, and generate more inquiries, without it taking up days of work.

At Komate, we help construction companies do exactly that: grow through smart, practical marketing. 

[Start today!](mailto:sofie.frodure@komate.be "Start today!")

# How Concrete Contractors Can Attract Better Jobs Without Spending More Time on Marketing

*   October 25, 2026

Between managing crews, ordering materials, preparing estimates, and keeping jobs on schedule, running a concrete company doesn’t leave much time for marketing.

And after spending the day on a job site, figuring out what to post on Facebook probably isn’t your top priority.

But here’s the challenge: Doing great work doesn’t automatically mean potential customers can find you.

Your competitors may not have better crews or equipment. They may simply be doing a better job of showing people what they offer. The good news? Marketing your concrete business doesn’t have to become another full-time job.

## Focus on Better Jobs, Not Just More Leads

More phone calls don’t always mean more profitable work. If your company specializes in driveway replacements, commercial slabs, or larger concrete projects, spending hours preparing estimates for jobs outside your preferred scope isn’t the best use of your time.

Your marketing should attract the work you actually want. Identify your most profitable services, preferred project types, and ideal service areas. Then make sure your website and advertising clearly communicate those priorities.

If driveway replacements are a priority, customers should easily find that service, see examples of your work, and know how to request an estimate.

The goal isn’t just getting more inquiries. It’s getting inquiries worth your time.

## Let Your Completed Projects Do the Marketing

Concrete contractors have a major advantage when it comes to marketing. Their work is visual.

A cracked driveway transformed into a smooth new surface, a completed shop slab, or a finished patio can demonstrate your experience better than a generic advertisement.

Before leaving a project, collect:

*   A photo before work begins.
*   A few photos of the crew or equipment in action.
*   A clear photo of the completed project.
*   The general location and type of work performed.
*   A quick explanation of what the customer needed.

Those photos can become social media posts, website portfolio features, or Google Business Profile updates. Your crew doesn’t have to become a team of content creators. A few photos and notes can go a long way. Learn more about [how employees can help create authentic marketing content](https://socialcreativeco.com/the-power-of-employee-generated-content-how-your-team-can-amplify-your-brand/).

You’re already doing the work. The opportunity is to make sure more people see it.

## Make Sure Customers Can Find You on Google

When someone needs a driveway replacement or a concrete slab for a backyard shop, there’s a good chance they’ll search Google for contractors nearby. If your business isn’t visible, potential customers may find someone else.

Your website should clearly explain your services, show where you work, and make requesting an estimate simple. Dedicated pages for important services can help customers find exactly what they’re looking for.

Your Google Business Profile should have accurate contact information, customer reviews, and recent project photos. It also helps to answer questions customers frequently ask, such as what affects driveway replacement costs or how long concrete takes to cure.

Understanding [why your Google Business Profile matters](https://socialcreativeco.com/google-business-profile-optimization/) is a good place to start.

## Real-World Example: Helping Low Country Concrete Get Found Online

Low Country Concrete serves Savannah, Richmond Hill, and nearby communities. Like most contractors, they’d rather focus on the work than the website. So we handle that part.

[](https://www.lowcountryconcrete.net/concrete-contractor-in-savannah-ga/)

**What we built for their Savannah page:**

### Location-specific content

A dedicated Savannah page featuring driveway replacements, patios, foundations, and commercial projects.

### Answers to common questions

Customers get answers before they pick up the phone.

### SEO details and internal links

Visitors find their way around the site, and requesting an estimate is simple.

That’s what effective marketing should do: make it easier for customers to find and choose your business, without adding more work to your day.

[See the Savannah Page](https://www.lowcountryconcrete.net/concrete-contractor-in-savannah-ga/)

## Build a Marketing Routine You Can Maintain

You don’t need to post every day or spend hours managing your online presence. Start with a simple routine.

### Each week:

*   Take photos of one completed or ongoing project.
*   Ask a satisfied customer for a Google review.
*   Share a project update or helpful tip.

### Each month:

*   Add project photos to your Google Business Profile.
*   Highlight a service you want to book more often.
*   Check that your website forms and phone links work.
*   Review where your inquiries are coming from.

Someone on your crew can collect photos while a marketing partner handles writing, graphics, website updates, and scheduling. Your marketing should be consistent, but it shouldn’t require your constant attention.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What’s the best way to market a concrete company?

Start with a professional website, an accurate Google Business Profile, customer reviews, and photos of completed projects. Local SEO and targeted advertising can help reach customers searching for your services.

### Do concrete contractors need to post on social media every day?

No, consistent posts featuring actual projects, useful advice, and your team’s work can help establish credibility without requiring daily content.

### Should I hire someone to handle my concrete company’s marketing?

If marketing consistently gets pushed aside while you’re managing projects, outsourcing may be worth considering. A marketing partner can help keep your website, social media, and local visibility efforts organized.

## You Handle the Concrete. We’ll Handle the Marketing.

You’ve invested in your equipment, built your crew, and worked hard to develop a reputation for quality. Your marketing should reflect that effort without requiring you to do everything yourself.
